english: It's raining outside.
tip: 비가 와요 (biga wayo) = 'rain comes' — how Korean says it's raining.

english: Do you have an umbrella?
tip: Everyday Korean says 'have' with 있어요 (isseoyo = exists): 우산 있어요? (usan isseoyo?) literally asks 'does an umbrella exist?'

english: It's snowing outside!
tip: 눈 (nun) = snow AND eye — context decides!

english: On Sundays I do nothing at all.
tip: 아무것도 (amugeotdo) + negative = nothing at all.

english: This weekend I'm going to rest up.
tip: 푹 쉬어요 (puk swieoyo) = rest deeply — wished to every tired friend.

english: I watched two movies at home.
tip: 편 (pyeon) counts movies and shows: 두 편 (du pyeon = two films).

english: Did you rest well over the weekend?
tip: Monday-morning Korean: 잘 쉬었어요? (jal swieosseoyo? = did you rest well?)

english: My phone battery is dead.
tip: 배터리가 없어요 (baeteoriga eopseoyo) = 'no battery' = my phone's dying.

english: I left my phone at home.
tip: 놓고 왔어요 (noko wasseoyo) = left it behind — the forgot-it phrase.

english: I KakaoTalk with my family every day.
tip: Add 하다 to anything: 카톡해요 (katokaeyo) = to message on KakaoTalk.

english: I took lots of photos at the Han River.
tip: You don't 'take' photos in Korean – you 찍다 (jjikda), the snap-a-shot verb: 사진을 많이 찍었어요 (sajineul mani jjigeosseoyo) = took lots of photos.

english: I took a selfie with my friend.
tip: 셀카 (selka) = 'self-camera' = selfie — a Konglish classic.

english: I make the bed every morning.
tip: 이불 (ibul) = blanket/bedding — you 'tidy' it, not 'make' it.

english: I made ramyeon in the evening.
tip: 끓여요 (kkeuryeoyo) = boil up: 라면을 끓여요 = make ramyeon.

english: Our home is the best place in the world.
tip: 제일 (jeil) = the most: 제일 좋아요 = like it best.

english: My head hurts so much.
tip: 아프다 → 아파요 (apayo): body part + 이/가 아파요 = my X hurts.

english: I have a fever.
tip: 열이 나요 (yeori nayo) = lit. a fever comes out — how Korean says "have a fever".

english: I am coughing a lot.
tip: 기침을 해요 (gichimeul haeyo) = lit. "do a cough" — symptoms pair with 하다.

english: I caught a cold.
tip: 감기에 걸렸어요 (gamgie geollyeosseoyo): catching a cold takes 에, not 을.

english: I ache all over from a cold.
tip: 몸살 (momsal) = the whole-body ache of a bad cold — it "breaks out": 났어요.

english: My stomach feels off.
tip: 속 (sok) = your insides: 속이 안 좋아요 = I feel queasy.

english: I have indigestion.
tip: X이/가 안 돼요 (an dwaeyo) = X does not work: 소화가 안 돼요.

english: My back hurts so much that I cannot get up.
tip: 못 (mot) before a verb = cannot: 못 일어나요 = can't get up.

english: My knee hurts, so stairs are hard.
tip: -아/어서 (-aseo) = because: 아파서 = because it hurts.

target: 속이 안 좋아서 토할 것 같아요.
english: My stomach is upset — I feel like throwing up.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 (geot gatayo) = feels like it will: 토할 것 같아요.

english: I am dizzy and I have a fever too.
tip: -고 (-go) also links two states with no time order – 어지럽고 열도 나요 (eojireopgo yeoldo nayo) is just 'dizzy and feverish', not one thing then another.

english: I could not sleep at night because of the cough.
tip: 때문에 (ttaemune) after a noun = because of: 기침 때문에.

english: I put in for sick leave with my department head.
tip: Titled superiors take 께 (kke), not 한테: 부장님께 = to the manager.

english: I will get a good rest at home today.
tip: -(으)ㄹ게요 (-lgeyo) = a promise to the listener: 쉴게요 = I'll rest, I promise.

english: The company president caught a cold too.
tip: Honored subjects take -시-: 걸리셨어요 (geollisyeosseoyo), never 걸렸어요.
